copy.method: Full recursive robocopy into a new reviewer-specific app directory

commands.kind: Additional read-only diagnostic; not counted as existing unit/integration tests
commands.note: The diagnostic completed successfully while detecting two HTTP 500 responses. Exit 0 does not mean those requests passed a correctness test.

actually_exercised: Valid login sets the student session, rotates CSRF and enables permanent expiry; logout clears authenticated access.
Wrong passwords fail without putting submitted credentials or IP addresses into the audit; five failures block the next login; a new app instance resets the process-local limiter.
SQL-like login payloads cannot establish a session or alter record counts.
Missing and forged CSRF tokens reject notice creation without insertion.
A student cannot edit/return another owner's notice or use a forged administrator role to remove it.
An owner creates, edits and marks a notice returned; data persists in the same SQLite database after constructing a fresh app instance. Forged owner/status form values are ignored.
Administrator deletion confirmation and cancellation are read-only; confirmed POST deletion removes the row and later detail returns 404.
Search treats SQL and LIKE metacharacters literally, and stored markup is escaped in browse/detail HTML.
Ten invalid form variants do not insert records: missing/overlong title, short description, empty location, invalid category/type, invalid or out-of-range dates.
Anonymous requests to selected browse/detail/form/removal routes redirect to login and cannot create notices.

Help requires authentication. Authenticated browse, baseline browse and help return HTML with at least two image elements, an alt attribute on each image, /static/ image paths and successful HTTP 200 image responses. Media test sets session user_id directly.
Additional read-only browse probes compare ordinary page/category filters with oversized integer values; captured stack traces identify integer conversion at SQLite parameter binding.

findings.title: Oversized browse filter numbers cause HTTP 500
findings.evidence: With an authenticated student test session, GET /?page=1152921504606846977 and GET /?category=9223372036854775808 each returned HTTP 500. Control requests page=2 and category=1 returned HTTP 200.
findings.cause: browse() accepts arbitrary Python integers. (page-1)*8 and int(category) can exceed SQLite's signed 64-bit integer range, causing uncaught OverflowError when bound to the query.
findings.impact: An authenticated user following or entering such a malformed filter URL receives a server error instead of a valid empty result or controlled validation response. The four diagnostic GETs left the copied main database unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Validate or bound page/category inputs before binding them to SQLite and add focused boundary regression cases.

limitations: This is an AI software review, not human usability research. No participant observations, success rates, task times or questionnaire scores were collected or invented.
No browser was used. Flask test-client checks do not establish visual layout, keyboard navigation, screen-reader behavior, responsive behavior, reduced-motion behavior or perceived usability.

Media checks assert only presence of alt attributes and successful static delivery. They do not judge alternative-text quality, decode/render image pixels, verify captions against images or measure transfer/performance improvements.
The assigned 15 tests do not exercise new-account registration or uploaded-photo lifecycle/validation. test_stage2_core.py contains related tests, but this reviewer did not run that suite.

The selected suites do not comprehensively verify combinations of category/status/My notices filters or pagination navigation; four supplemental read-only requests only probe a narrow numeric boundary.
Persistence is checked with a fresh Flask application instance and the same database, not an operating-system process restart or deployed multi-process server.
No external email client was opened and no message was sent. The Contact author link was inspected in the detail template only.
Tests ran against an isolated local Windows portable-Python copy; this does not verify Linux or a network deployment.
